note: Reported NEDFABS cases consistently present with developmental delay, intellectual disability, and structural brain anomalies (e.g., cerebellar atrophy), indicating that normal neurodevelopment or MRI strongly argues against the diagnosis.

evidence.text: All four described patients with biallelic GTF3C3 variants presented with developmental delay, intellectual disability, and abnormal brain imaging showing brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement and frontal lobe hypoplasia.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: The patients exhibited microcephaly, developmental delay, intellectual disability and distinctive dysmorphic facies that appear recognizable in very young children. Their brain imaging showed brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement, as well as hypoplasia of the frontal lobes and one patient had moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern.

evidence.text: Brain MRI confirmed marked anomalies in the oldest reported patient, consistent with the neurodevelopmental and brain malformation syndrome phenotype described across GTF3C3-related disorder cohorts.

source.title: Case report: Characterization of a patient with novel biallelic variants in GTF3C3 and comprehensive review of previously reported cases
